user.title: Opus GreenNet Bridge
user.description: Connect to the OPUS gateway in your network. Home Assistant talks to it directly over its REST API; no MQTT broker is needed. A gateway found in the local network is filled in automatically.

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the OPUS gateway in your network.
data_description.port: Port of the gateway's REST API: 8080 for gateways before WebUI 2026. A gateway with WebUI 2026 is recognised automatically and uses port 443 (HTTPS).
data_description.username: API user of the gateway (admin by default). For a gateway with WebUI 2026 enter a user of its web interface (role admin or installer).
data_description.password: API password. For gateways before WebUI 2026 this is by default the gateway's EURID in capital letters, as printed on the gateway. For a gateway with WebUI 2026 enter the password of that user; Home Assistant never creates users on the gateway.

reauth_confirm.title: Connect to gateway {eag_id}
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the address and API credentials of gateway {eag_id}. Gateways set up with an earlier version of this integration were connected through MQTT; this version connects to the gateway directly. The gateway could not be found in the local network with its default credentials, so enter its address once, or the password if you changed it. All devices and entities are kept.

data_description.password: API password. For gateways before WebUI 2026 this is by default the gateway's EURID in capital letters, as printed on the gateway. For a gateway with WebUI 2026 enter the password of that user; Home Assistant never creates users on the gateway.

certificate.title: Confirm the gateway certificate
certificate.description: Gateway {eag_id} presents a different certificate than the one remembered at the first connection. This happens after a factory reset or when the gateway was replaced, but also when another device answers at this address. Nothing was sent to it. Fingerprint (SHA-256): {fingerprint}. Continue only if you expect the change.

certificate_new.title: Confirm the gateway certificate
certificate_new.description: The gateway at {host} uses WebUI 2026 and presents a self-signed certificate that Home Assistant cannot check. It will be remembered, and later connections accept only this certificate. Nothing was sent to the gateway yet. Fingerprint (SHA-256): {fingerprint}. Continue only if this is your gateway; compare the fingerprint with the one in the gateway's web interface if you can.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the gateway. Check the host and port.
error.invalid_host: Enter only the gateway's IP address or host name, without http://, port or path.
error.host_not_local: Enter an address in your local network (private, link-local, VPN or the network Home Assistant is in). The gateway only speaks unencrypted HTTP, so public addresses are not supported. If a host name fails, enter the gateway's IPv4 address.
error.invalid_auth: The gateway rejected the username or password.
error.unsupported_gateway: The device at this address did not answer like an OPUS gateway.
error.wrong_gateway: This address belongs to a different gateway than {eag_id}.

abort.already_configured: This gateway is already configured. Its connection settings were updated.
abort.not_ipv4_address: Only gateways with an IPv4 address are supported.
abort.not_local_address: The announced address is not in the local network and is ignored.

init.title: Write access to device settings
init.description:
**Caution: These settings are written directly to the actuator.**

Incorrect values can:

- cause malfunctions or device failure
- damage the actuator or connected equipment

Only enable write access if you understand the effects of the changes.

data.allow_setting_writes: I understand the risks and want to enable write access.

data_description.allow_setting_writes: Applies to all devices of this gateway. Reading settings is not affected.

non_local_gateway_address.title: The gateway address is not in the local network
non_local_gateway_address.description:
The address of this gateway is outside the local network. The gateway only speaks unencrypted HTTP, so its login can be read on the way. The integration keeps working, but re-authentication and reconfiguration only accept a local address.

Open the Opus GreenNet Bridge integration, choose Reconfigure from its menu and enter the gateway's address in your local network, or reach the gateway through a VPN. The notice disappears when the integration is loaded again with a local address.

confirm.title: Update references to {removed_entity_id}
confirm.description:
While adopting the upstream unique IDs, the integration found two registry entries for the same device and gateway. It kept your existing entity {preserved_entity_id} with its entity ID, name and settings, and removed the duplicate entity {removed_entity_id}.

Automations, scripts, scenes and dashboards that still use {removed_entity_id} no longer work. Replace that entity ID with {preserved_entity_id}, then select Submit to dismiss this message. Nothing is sent to the gateway or the device.

write_access_off.title: Write access to device settings is not enabled
write_access_off.description:
An entity that changes a device setting of {name} is enabled, but write access is not. Changes are refused until you enable write access: open Settings → Devices & services → Opus GreenNet, choose Configure and confirm the warning.

Write access allows device configuration to be written directly to the actuator. Incorrect settings may cause malfunctions, device failure, or damage to connected equipment. The notice disappears when write access is enabled or the entity is disabled again.
